text: [La Jolla Beach & Tennis Club, Inc. v. Industrial Indem. Co., supra, 9 C4th at 42-43, 36 CR2d at 108-109; see also Transamerica Ins. Co. v. Sup.Ct. (Western Industrial Mgmt. Corp.) (1994) 29 CA4th 1705, 1715, 35 CR2d 259, 264] b. [3:562] Immaterial that same facts involved in both WCAB proceedings and civil action: The fact the civil action may adjudicate facts at issue in the workers' compensation proceeding does not create a potential for coverage under the workers' compensation insurance: “[T]he test is whether the underlying action for which defense and indemnity is sought potentially seeks relief within the coverage of the policy.” [La Jolla Beach & Tennis Club, Inc. v. Industrial Indem. Co., supra, 9 C4th at 44, 36 CR2d at 110 (emphasis in original)] Cross-refer: Workers' compensation insurance is discussed further in Croskey, Heeseman, Ehrlich & Klee, Cal. Prac. Guide: Insurance Litigation (TRG), Ch. 7G. [3:563 - 3:574] Reserved. 4
